agent.description: Agent: per-node DaemonSet that watches the MXL domain via fanotify, publishes flow state, and serves the LD_PRELOAD intent socket.

runAsNonRoot.description: fanotify on /run/mxl/domain reads host inodes, so the agent currently runs as root. PSA-restricted environments cannot host the agent without a policy exception.
runAsNonRoot.title: runAsNonRoot

kubeApiBurst.description: Client-side burst above kubeApiQps. 0 leaves the client-go default in place.
kubeApiBurst.title: kubeApiBurst

kubeApiQps.description: Client-side request rate to the API server. A node holding many flows spends one Get and one Update per flow per renewal pass; at the client-go default of 5 the loop blocks rather than fails, stretching past the Lease duration it exists to keep fresh. 0 leaves the client-go default in place.
kubeApiQps.title: kubeApiQps

provider.description: Explicit libmxl-fabrics provider stamped onto on-demand (intent-driven) mirrors, bypassing per-node resolution. Empty (or "auto") resolves a concrete provider from the source and target nodes' MxlNodeCapabilities; set a concrete value to force one cluster-wide.
provider.title: provider

shimPath.description: Where the agent drops the copy of libmxl-intent.so its image carries, on every start. A consumer that already mounts hostPath.run for the intent socket preloads the shim from there instead of copying it out of the carrier image with an initContainer. Keep the path under hostPath.run, or consumer pods cannot see it. Empty disables the drop.
shimPath.title: shimPath

hostPID.description: Run the agent in the host PID namespace. Required for the intent socket's SO_PEERCRED-based pod identification: without it the connecting consumer pod's PID is not visible to the agent and the on-demand mirror materialization path silently fails.
hostPID.title: hostPID

hostPath.description: hostPath layout. The agent mounts the whole /run/mxl so the intent socket lands on the host where consumer pods can see it.
hostPath.title: hostPath

tag.description: Image tag. Empty defaults to the chart appVersion prefixed with "v": the agent image is released under the chart version. Set this or image.digest.
tag.title: tag

agent.title: agent

cleanup.description: Pre-delete lifecycle hooks. The domain wipe removes stale .mxl-flow directories under gateway.flags.domainPath at chart uninstall, because they live on a hostPath and survive namespace and CRD teardown.

enabled.description: Wipe stale .mxl-flow directories under gateway.flags.domainPath during helm uninstall, closing the cold-reinstall lifecycle bug where surviving hostPath state from a prior install causes the agent classifier to default the dirs to Origin on the next install (ghost source-side initiator).  Set to false if either applies:   - producers (libmxl writers) are still mmap-attached to files     under domainPath at uninstall time. rm -rf does not crash     producers (mmap regions survive unlink), but their writes     are orphaned from any new consumer. Drain producers first,     then uninstall.   - host state under domainPath is intentionally reused across     chart reinstalls (advanced; expect to clean up manually to     avoid the ghost-initiator bug).
enabled.title: enabled

guardImage.description: Image used by the nodecount-guard init-container. Must carry a kubectl binary on PATH.
guardImage.title: guardImage

image.description: Image used by the cleanup Job. Pinned tag (no :latest).
image.title: image

nodeCount.description: Effective node count for the agent DaemonSet. An under-set value yields a partial wipe; the nodecount-guard init-container fails the chart with a clear error in that case.
nodeCount.title: nodeCount

cleanup.title: cleanup

crds.description: CRD handling. The chart installs CRDs from its crds/ directory by default. Helm only installs them on first install and never deletes or upgrades them; Flux's HelmRelease.spec.{install,upgrade}.crds governs replace semantics. Set skipInstall=true when CRDs are managed by a separate Kustomization or operator framework.
crds.title: crds

dashboards.description: for Grafana's dashboard sidecar to discover.

annotations.description: Annotations on the ConfigMaps. grafana_folder places the dashboard when the sidecar runs with folderAnnotation set.
annotations.title: annotations

datasourceUid.description: uid of the Prometheus datasource the panels query. The default is what kube-prometheus-stack names its own; a Grafana provisioned otherwise states its uid here.
datasourceUid.title: datasourceUid

labels.description: Labels the sidecar selects on. A deployment configured with a non-empty sidecar labelValue, or selecting on a release label, sets its own here.
labels.title: labels

namespace.description: Namespace to place the ConfigMaps in. Empty uses the release namespace. The sidecar's searchNamespace defaults to the namespace Grafana runs in, so a Grafana installed elsewhere needs either that setting widened or this pointed at it.
namespace.title: namespace

dashboards.title: dashboards

exporter.description: serves Prometheus metrics for every flow materialized on it. A domain is shared by every pod on its node, so one DaemonSet covers the node and reports each flow once; a second reader of the same domain would only repeat it.

args.description: Extra raw args appended after the rendered flags.
args.title: args

domainPath.description: Absolute path of the MXL domain directory to report on. Must resolve to the same domain the agent watches, below hostPath.run.
domainPath.title: domainPath

flowLifetime.description: How long a departed flow keeps being exported with mxl_flow_present at 0, so a flow that ends between two scrapes leaves a record rather than a gap. One sweep of gateway.flags.domainGcInterval, so the metric set describes the domain as it is rather than as it was.
flowLifetime.title: flowLifetime

scanPeriod.description: How often the domain directory is re-listed for flows that appeared or disappeared. Scrapes read the cache this maintains.
scanPeriod.title: scanPeriod

hostPath.description: hostPath layout. The exporter mounts the runtime root read-only; it opens libmxl flow readers and never writes into the domain.
hostPath.title: hostPath

digest.description: Image digest. Wins over tag when set. @schema pattern: ^$|^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$ @schema
digest.title: digest

tag.description: Image tag. Empty defaults to the chart appVersion prefixed with "v": the exporter image is released under the chart version. Set this or image.digest.
tag.title: tag

enabled.description: Create a ServiceMonitor. Requires the monitoring.coreos.com CRDs to be installed cluster-wide.
enabled.title: enabled

name.description: ServiceAccount name. Empty falls back to the generated name.
name.title: name

enabled.description: Publish mxl_flow_location_info from the MxlFlow CRs. That is what names the producing node (phase Origin), so dashboards do not need media functions to label themselves. Disabling it drops the metric and the exporter's only API access.
enabled.title: enabled

exporter.title: exporter

gateway.description: Gateway: per-node DaemonSet that owns libmxl-fabrics handles and moves grains across the wire. Runs with hostNetwork so the fabric endpoint binds the node interface.

add.description: Additional caps beyond what rdma.enabled implies.
add.title: add

bindAddress.description: Bind address for libmxl-fabrics endpoints. Default uses the downward-API POD_IP so each gateway binds its node IP. An explicit empty string ("") emits `--bind-address=` (bare equals), which suppresses the POD_IP fallback so libfabric picks the interface; useful when the gateway runs on a Multus-attached NAD and the RDMA fabric is a secondary netdev.
bindAddress.title: bindAddress

degradedAfter.description: Grain-commit inactivity after which the target gateway demotes a mirror to Degraded. Same threshold gates the Reconcile fast-path so a stale Ready status falls through to re-establish.
degradedAfter.title: degradedAfter

domainGcGrace.description: How long after start the first reclaim sweep is held back. A restarted gateway has no writer attached to the mirror copies it was serving, and a consumer's reader does not protect them, so a sweep inside this window would delete flows consumers are still reading and the reconciler is about to re-establish. Must outlast the reconciler's re-establish path.
domainGcGrace.title: domainGcGrace

domainGcInterval.description: How often libmxl reclaims flow directories no writer holds. The criterion is libmxl's own: a writer keeps a shared lock for as long as it is attached, so a live producer or mirror writer is never a candidate however long since its last grain. Set to 0 to disable reclaiming.
domainGcInterval.title: domainGcInterval

domainGcScaffoldGrace.description: How old a half-built flow directory must be before it is reclaimed. libmxl builds a flow under a temporary name and renames it into place, removing it on every unwinding exit, so only a death that skips unwinding leaves one -- and libmxl's own collection walks published flows, so nothing sees it afterwards. A producer SIGKILLed part way through allocating its ring therefore leaves the whole allocation in the shared domain, at the node's expense rather than its own. Whether a writer still holds the scaffold is decided by the same lock libmxl uses; this only spans the moment between the data file being created and locked. Negative disables it.
domainGcScaffoldGrace.title: domainGcScaffoldGrace

fabricCidr.description: CIDRs the fabric interfaces must fall inside. Empty considers every address libmxl-fabrics reports, which on a node with several NICs includes the ones carrying ST 2110 essence, cluster traffic, or out-of-band management. Set this to the subnet of the MXL fabric to keep mirrors off them. Applies to both what a node advertises and what a mirror binds.
fabricCidr.title: fabricCidr

fabricDevice.description: Device names the fabric interfaces must match, as the provider names them (the kernel netdev name for tcp, the NIC name libfabric reports otherwise). Empty considers every device. Useful where the fabric shares a subnet with other traffic.
fabricDevice.title: fabricDevice

fabricMinLinkSpeed.description: Minimum link speed a fabric interface must report, as a quantity in bits per second (for example 25G). Empty imposes no floor. An interface whose provider reports no link speed is rejected when this is set, which includes interfaces with no physical NIC behind them.
fabricMinLinkSpeed.title: fabricMinLinkSpeed

kubeApiBurst.description: Client-side burst above kubeApiQps. 0 leaves the client-go default in place.
kubeApiBurst.title: kubeApiBurst

kubeApiQps.description: Client-side request rate to the API server. A node holding many flows spends one Get and one Update per flow per renewal pass; at the client-go default of 5 the loop blocks rather than fails, stretching past the Lease duration it exists to keep fresh. 0 leaves the client-go default in place.
kubeApiQps.title: kubeApiQps

pacingChunks.description: How many slice ranges a paced grain is split into. Read only while pacingFraction is positive. This sets how short the individual bursts get: the contiguous burst is one grain divided by this, and switch buffer occupancy follows that length. Each range costs one cgo call and, because a partial range leaves libmxl-fabrics's one-write-per-grain fast path, one RMA write per plane. Raise it if the switch still reports drops at a pacing fraction you are happy with; lower it if gateway CPU is the constraint. Capped by the grain's slice count, so a flow with fewer slices than this uses one range per slice. Under 2 disables pacing.
pacingChunks.title: pacingChunks

pacingFraction.description: How much of a grain's own interval the source gateway spreads that grain's transmission over, instead of handing the fabric a whole grain the NIC then drains at line rate. Negative disables pacing and restores whole-grain transfers, which is the default: the burst is only worth shaping where a receiver loses grains to it, and where nothing is lost the added latency and the per-chunk cost buy nothing. Turn it on when a receiver several flows converge on reports drops well below nominal link utilisation, which is the signature of overlapping bursts rather than of offered load. Peak rate becomes the flow's own rate divided by this, so 0.5 halves the burst and doubles its length, and is where to start. The cost is latency: a grain completes at the receiver up to this much of its interval later. Depends on the flow's edit rate alone, never on the link speed, so one value holds from 25GbE to EFA. Raise it toward 1 while drops remain; lower it when the added latency matters more than the burst. Must stay below 1, or a grain's transmission runs into the next one.
pacingFraction.title: pacingFraction

pprofBindAddress.description: Bind address for the net/http/pprof endpoint. Empty disables; otherwise must be a loopback bind (127.0.0.1: or localhost:). Use kubectl port-forward to reach the endpoint; see docs/diagnostics/perf-shortfall.md for the capture recipe.
pprofBindAddress.title: pprofBindAddress

probePeriod.description: Shortest interval between two libmxl-fabrics interface enumerations. Status still refreshes every resyncPeriod from the last result. Each enumeration sweeps every provider libfabric was built with and warns about those it finds no device for.
probePeriod.title: probePeriod

providers.description: Upper bound on the libmxl-fabrics providers a gateway may advertise and use. Each node publishes this list intersected with what libmxl-fabrics finds on it, so `any` advertises the hardware that is present and nothing else. Narrow it to keep a provider out of consideration on every node.
providers.title: providers

rdmaEnumerationGrace.description: How long that discrepancy holds before the probe fails. Measured across consecutive enumerations, so it spans several probePeriod rather than letting one decide it.
rdmaEnumerationGrace.title: rdmaEnumerationGrace

rdmaEnumerationLiveness.description: Fail the liveness probe while the host exposes RDMA devices that no enumerated provider accounts for. libfabric fixes a provider's device list at the first enumeration, so a gateway that started before the hardware was usable never revisits it and only a restart does. Off by default: a node whose devices the built providers cannot drive reports the same discrepancy, and there a restart loops instead of recovering. The RDMADevicesEnumerated condition reports the state either way.
rdmaEnumerationLiveness.title: rdmaEnumerationLiveness

readerStallAfter.description: How long a source-side reader may report an unchanged head index, having never transferred a grain, before SourceProgress reports ReaderNotAdvancing.
readerStallAfter.title: readerStallAfter

hostNetwork.description: hostNetwork is required because the libmxl-fabrics TargetInfo embeds the host:port a peer dials; a CNI overlay IP would not be reachable cross-node.
hostNetwork.title: hostNetwork

tag.description: Image tag. Empty defaults to the chart appVersion prefixed with "v": the gateway image is released under the chart version. Set this or image.digest.
tag.title: tag

enabled.description: Add the capabilities the verbs/efa providers need (IPC_LOCK, SYS_RESOURCE; libmxl pins shm pages).
enabled.title: enabled

infinibandHostPathType.description: hostPath type for the InfiniBand mount. `Directory` holds the pod in ContainerCreating on a node where the path is absent, which is a deliberate failure on a DaemonSet that is only meant to run on RDMA-capable nodes, and a hang on one that is not.
infinibandHostPathType.title: infinibandHostPathType

mountInfiniband.description: Bind-mount the host's InfiniBand device directory into the gateway. Only consulted when rdma.enabled is set. A bind mount alone does not pass the cgroup-v2 device controller, so a node whose devices come from a device plugin wants this off and `resourceName` set instead.
mountInfiniband.title: mountInfiniband

resourceName.description: Extended-resource name advertised by a Kubernetes device plugin. `devic.es/rdma` from generic-device-plugin and `rdma/hca_shared_devices` from k8s-rdma-shared-dev-plugin cover on-prem verbs; `vpc.amazonaws.com/efa` from aws-efa-k8s-device-plugin covers EFA; a site may advertise something else entirely. When non-empty, the gateway container gets `<resourceName>: 1` on both requests and limits. Empty disables the request.  The request is what grants the container its cgroup device permissions, and it also makes the pod unschedulable on any node not advertising the resource -- which is why a cluster with mixed hardware needs `gateway.variants` rather than one DaemonSet.
resourceName.title: resourceName

variants.description: Render the gateway DaemonSet once per enabled entry instead of once, for a cluster whose nodes do not all carry the same fabric hardware. With nothing enabled -- the default -- exactly one DaemonSet renders from the values above, which is what a uniform cluster wants.  Keys name the variant and suffix the DaemonSet name, so they have to be DNS-1123 labels. Entries beyond the three below are allowed; each may override any key under `gateway`, with maps merging key by key against the values above and lists replacing wholesale.  Placement is deliberately unset on every entry. Which label marks a node's fabric is a site's choice, and a default here would not be replaced by a downstream override but merged with it, leaving a nodeSelector that demands both labels and matches no node.  Enabling two or more entries means declaring their placement, and the placements have to be complementary: two gateways on one node open the same MXL domain, reconcile the same mirrors, and write the same MxlNodeCapabilities, which is named after the node. Helm cannot read node labels, so it rejects only the combinations that guarantee overlap. Keying every variant on a distinct value of one label is what makes overlap impossible; a class defined by the absence of that label needs `affinity` with `DoesNotExist`, which a nodeSelector cannot express. See docs/RDMA.md.

efa.description: resource name cluster-wide, so that one is filled in. EFA node groups are conventionally tainted with the same key, which a variant selecting them has to tolerate.
efa.title: efa

verbs.description: plugin advertises the device is a site's choice (`devic.es/rdma` from generic-device-plugin, `rdma/hca_shared_devices` from k8s-rdma-shared-dev-plugin).
verbs.title: verbs

variants.title: variants
